items.title: GeNor
items.text:
GeNor lets Claude (and Codex, opencode, or you at a terminal) take GWAS summary statistics from QC to genetic correlation, Mendelian randomisation, pleiotropy, fine-mapping, colocalisation and gene-level follow-up, with a reproducible record of every step. It installs with nothing but uv.

Research use only

GeNor is research software for academic use. It is not a medical device and must not be used for clinical decisions, diagnosis, or commercial services.

items.title: Quick install
items.text:
Claude CodeCommand lineClaude Desktop, Codex, opencode 
/plugin marketplace add amanzadi/GeNor
/plugin install genor@genor

This installs the GeNor skills, the MCP server and slash commands, and puts genor on Claude's PATH. Then ask, in a folder with your files:

Estimate the genetic correlation and causal effect of BMI on depression from bmi.tsv.gz and mdd.tsv.gz.

curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh                  # uv, if you don't have it
uvx --from git+https://github.com/amanzadi/GeNor genor doctor    # until the PyPI release

After the PyPI release this becomes uvx genor doctor or uv tool install genor.

All use the same MCP server (genor mcp). Copy-paste configs for each client are on the install page.

Linux and macOS (x86-64 and Apple silicon); on Windows use WSL. Python ≥ 3.11, which uv installs for you.

items.title: A first run
items.text:
GeNor ships a simulated GWAS pair (not real data) with a planted causal effect of 0.15 and a genetic correlation of 0.15.

genor example --out ex
genor sumstats load ex/bmi_sim.tsv.gz --trait BMI_sim --ancestry EUR --out runs/bmi
genor sumstats load ex/mdd_sim.tsv.gz --trait MDD_sim --ancestry EUR \
      --population-prevalence 0.15 --out runs/mdd
genor refdata fetch ldsc-ldscores-eur ldsc-weights-eur          # 25 MB
genor ldsc rg runs/bmi runs/mdd --out runs/rg
genor backend install plink2 && genor refdata fetch g1000-eur --yes   # 288 MB LD panel
genor mr run --exposure runs/bmi --outcome runs/mdd --overlap none --out runs/mr
genor report build runs/bmi runs/mdd runs/rg runs/mr --out report.md
Estimate (truth) LDSC rg 0.142, SE 0.032 (0.15) MR, IVW, 141 instruments 0.136, SE 0.018 (0.15) Weighted median / weighted mode 0.147 / 0.152 Flags raised heterogeneity, directional pleiotropy (3 pleiotropic instruments were planted)

items.title: Why GeNor
items.text:
• Summary statistics only

    GeNor refuses individual-level genotype data. You bring your own GWAS files; GeNor tells you where to find them but never downloads GWAS or handles tokens.

  • Agent-first

    Every command prints one JSON object with a short summary, structured warnings, and the questions the agent must put to you. Bulk results go to files, not into the agent's context.

  • Guard rails in code

    Build and ancestry mismatches against an LD panel are errors. Palindromic SNPs, allele flips, MHC, inflation and sample overlap are checked and reported.

  • Reproducible

    Each run writes manifest.json: input checksums, parameters, tool and data versions, warnings, and the citations to use.

  • Validated

    Native reimplementations are tested against TwoSampleMR, coloc, R meta and the original LDSC. See validation.

  • Nothing to set up

    One tool, uv, installs everything. Reference data and PLINK 2 are downloaded on request, checksum-pinned, and only after you agree.

items.title: What is included
items.text:
Area Methods Summary statistics load common formats (GWAS-VCF, PLINK 2, REGENIE, SAIGE, METAL, FinnGen), QC, build inference, liftover, Manhattan/QQ Meta-analysis fixed-effect IVW, DerSimonian-Laird random effects, Q, I², sample-size weighted Z Heritability, rg LDSC h2 (observed and liability scale) and genetic correlation Loci LD clumping against 1000 Genomes with PLINK 2 Mendelian randomisation IVW, MR-Egger, weighted median, weighted/simple mode, Steiger, leave-one-out, STROBE-MR checklist Pleiotropy condFDR / conjFDR through the pleioFDR Python port Fine-mapping, colocalisation Wakefield ABF credible sets, coloc ABF (H0–H4) Gene analysis MAGMA gene, gene-set, gene-property (user-installed MAGMA) Lookups Open Targets Platform, Ensembl VEP, STRING, g:Profiler Reports Markdown + HTML combining runs, warnings, decisions and references

Defaults and the reasoning behind them are on the methods page; what is not in GeNor yet is on the roadmap.

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
One package, three layers. The CLI is the core; the MCP server and skills sit on top of it.

src/genor/
  cli.py            Typer app; every command can print JSON and writes a run directory
  commands.py       command implementations shared by the CLI and MCP server
  mcp_server.py     fastmcp server; analyses run as background jobs
  runs.py           run directory + manifest.json (inputs, sha256, params, versions, citations)
  jobs.py           detached subprocess jobs: submit / status / result / logs / cancel
  errors.py         GenorError (code + hint), NeedsUserDecision (exit 3), structured warnings
  guards.py         summary-statistics-only refusal, build/ancestry checks
  config.py         platform data/config/state dirs (GENOR_HOME overrides)
  skills.py         locate, serve (get_guidance) and install skills
  sumstats/         columns.py, load.py, qc.py, harmonise.py, liftover.py, sources.toml
  refdata/          registry.toml + checksum-pinned lazy downloads
  backends/         registry.toml + resolver/installer for external tools
  methods/          meta, ldsc (+ vendored _ldsc), clump, mr, pleio, coloc (ABF), magma
  lookup/           http.py (rate limits, retries, test transport), services.py
  report/           plots.py, strobe_mr.py, builder.py (Markdown + HTML)
  data/             build_markers.tsv.gz, example/ (simulated GWAS pair)
skills/             SKILL.md trees (Claude Code plugin reads them here; copied into the wheel)
.claude-plugin/     plugin.json + marketplace.json
.mcp.json, bin/, commands/   plugin MCP config, PATH wrapper, slash commands

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
• genor <area> <verb> ... --out <run_dir> --json. Stdout carries one short JSON object (status, summary, warnings, ask_user, files, next_steps); tables and figures go to the run directory.
  • Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 actionable error (error.code, error.hint), 3 the human must decide (error.ask_user), 1 unexpected failure.
  • A loaded trait is a directory with sumstats.parquet (GWAS-SSF column names) and sumstats.json (build, ancestry, N, cases/controls, prevalences, column mapping, QC report). All analyses take trait directories, never raw files.
  • Warnings have a stable code and a severity (info, warning, serious); skills map codes to meanings and fixes.
  • The MCP server never blocks longer than ~50 s: it submits a job, waits, and returns either the result or a job id (Codex's default tool timeout is 60 s).

items.title: Decisions
items.text:
• Summary statistics only and no authenticated fetching: GeNor never handles credentials or individual-level data; it points users to sources.
  • uv core + opt-in backends: everything in core works from uvx genor; tools that are R-only, container-only or not redistributable are optional and detected by genor doctor.
  • Native ports only with golden tests against the reference implementation.
  • GPL-3 because LDSC is vendored.

items.title: genor sumstats sources

Where to find GWAS summary statistics (GeNor never downloads them itself).

  • NAME

items.title: genor sumstats load
items.text:
Parse a summary statistics file (any common format, GWAS-VCF), standardise, QC, plot.

  • FILE
  • --trait: Short trait name, e.g. BMI.
  • --out, -o: Run directory to write (created).
  • --build: GRCh37 or GRCh38 (inferred if omitted).
  • --ancestry: EUR, EAS, AFR, AMR, SAS, MID, CSA, or multi.
  • --n: Total sample size if not in the file.
  • --n-cases: Number of cases (binary traits).
  • --n-controls: Number of controls (binary traits).
  • --population-prevalence: For liability-scale h2.
  • --effect-type: beta or or (odds ratio).
  • --col: Column override canonical=FILECOL, repeatable.
  • --maf: Minimum MAF. (default: 0.01)
  • --info: Minimum imputation INFO. (default: 0.8)
  • --drop-mhc, --no-drop-mhc: Remove chr6:25-34 Mb (default: keep and flag).
  • --plots, --no-plots: Write Manhattan and QQ plots. (default: True)

items.title: genor clump
items.text: LD clumping into independent loci.

items.title: genor clump run
items.text:
Clump a trait into independent index variants.

  • TRAIT
  • --out, -o: Run directory to write (created).
  • --mode: plink (LD panel) or distance (no LD; approximate) (default: plink)
  • --preset: loci (r2 0.1, 250 kb) or mr (r2 0.001, 10 Mb) (default: loci)
  • --p1: Index p-value threshold (preset default 5e-8)
  • --r2: LD r2 threshold (preset default)
  • --kb: Window in kb (preset default)
  • --panel: refdata name, e.g. g1000-eur

items.title: genor mr
items.text: Two-sample Mendelian randomisation with STROBE-MR report.

items.title: genor mr run
items.text:
Instrument selection, harmonisation, IVW/Egger/median/mode, diagnostics, plots, STROBE-MR.

  • --exposure: Loaded exposure trait directory.
  • --outcome: Loaded outcome trait directory.
  • --out, -o: Run directory to write (created).
  • --p-threshold: Instrument p-value threshold. (default: 5e-08)
  • --clump-mode: plink or distance (default: plink)
  • --panel: LD panel refdata name (default from ancestry, e.g. g1000-eur)
  • --clump-r2: Clumping r2 for instruments (default: 0.001)
  • --clump-kb: Clumping window (kb) (default: 10000)
  • --instruments: File whose first column lists instrument rsIDs.
  • --exclude-mhc, --no-exclude-mhc: Drop instruments in chr6:25-34 Mb (default: keep)
  • --overlap: Sample overlap stated by the user: none|partial|substantial|unknown
  • --nboot: Bootstrap replicates (weighted median/mode SE) (default: 1000)
  • --seed: Random seed (default: 1)

  • --seed: (default: 1)
  • --keep-mhc, --no-keep-mhc: Do not exclude the MHC

items.title: Where to find GWAS summary statistics
items.text: Generated from src/genor/sumstats/sources.toml (also genor sumstats sources). GeNor never downloads GWAS: you download the file, accept the provider's terms, and give GeNor the local path. Checked 2026-11-25; services change.

items.title: NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog (summary statistics) (gwas-catalog)
items.text:
• URL: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/downloads/summary-statistics
  • FTP: https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gwas/summary_statistics/
  • Access: Open. Files by study accession (GCST...). The old summary-statistics REST API and REST API v1 are retired; browse the website or FTP.
  • Format: GWAS-SSF (harmonised *.h.tsv.gz files are GRCh38) and submitter formats
  • Build: Harmonised files: GRCh38. Check each study.
  • Good for: Any trait; first place to look.
  • Cite: Cite the original study (PubMed ID on the study page) and the GWAS Catalog (Cerezo et al. 2025, NAR).

items.title: Psychiatric Genomics Consortium (pgc)
items.text:
• URL: https://pgc.unc.edu/for-researchers/download-results/
  • Access: Free after agreeing to terms of use on the website (per dataset). Some datasets exclude 23andMe or require a separate request.
  • Format: Mostly PLINK/ricopili style text, GRCh37
  • Build: GRCh37
  • Good for: Psychiatric disorders (MDD, SCZ, BIP, ADHD, ASD, PTSD, ...).
  • Cite: Cite the paper listed for each download and follow PGC's acknowledgement rules.

items.title: IEU OpenGWAS (opengwas)
items.text:
• URL: https://opengwas.io
  • Access: Needs a free account and a personal JWT token for API use; files can be downloaded as GWAS-VCF per study ID. Token handling stays with the user, never in GeNor.
  • Format: GWAS-VCF (GeNor reads single-trait GWAS-VCF directly)
  • Build: GRCh37
  • Good for: Large harmonised collection, popular for MR.
  • Cite: Cite the original study and Elsworth et al. 2020 (bioRxiv 10.1101/2020.08.10.244293).

items.title: FinnGen public results (finngen)
items.text:
• URL: https://www.finngen.fi/en/access_results
  • Access: Open after filling a short form; per-release bucket of per-endpoint files.
  • Format: Tab-separated, GRCh38, columns #chrom pos ref alt rsids nearest_genes pval mlogp beta sebeta af_alt ...
  • Build: GRCh38
  • Good for: Disease endpoints from Finnish registries; Finnish (EUR, isolate) ancestry.
  • Cite: Kurki MI et al. FinnGen provides genetic insights from a well-phenotyped isolated population. Nature 2023.

items.title: Pan-UK Biobank (pan-ukb)
items.text:
• URL: https://pan.ukbb.broadinstitute.org/downloads
  • Access: Open (AWS open data).
  • Format: Tab-separated per phenotype with per-ancestry columns (EUR, AFR, AMR, CSA, EAS, MID). Pick one ancestry's columns with --col.
  • Build: GRCh37
  • Good for: Thousands of UK Biobank phenotypes across six ancestry groups.
  • Cite: Pan-UKB team, https://pan.ukbb.broadinstitute.org (2020); cite UK Biobank.

items.title: Neale lab UK Biobank GWAS (neale-ukb)
items.text:
• URL: http://www.nealelab.is/uk-biobank
  • Access: Open.
  • Format: Tab-separated, GRCh37, variant as chr:pos:ref:alt
  • Build: GRCh37
  • Good for: Many UK Biobank traits, EUR.
  • Cite: Neale lab UK Biobank GWAS round 2 (2018).

items.title: GIANT consortium (anthropometric traits) (giant)
items.text:
• URL: https://portals.broadinstitute.org/collaboration/giant/index.php/GIANT_consortium_data_files
  • Access: Open.
  • Format: Text, GRCh37
  • Build: GRCh37
  • Good for: BMI, height, waist-hip ratio.
  • Cite: Cite the specific GIANT paper (e.g. Yengo et al. 2018 for BMI/height).

items.title: eQTLGen (blood cis/trans-eQTL) (eqtlgen)
items.text:
• URL: https://www.eqtlgen.org/phase1.html
  • Access: Open.
  • Format: Text; SMR .besd versions available
  • Build: GRCh37
  • Good for: Exposure data for SMR/MR on gene expression.
  • Cite: Vosa U et al. Nat Genet 2021.

items.title: GTEx portal (eQTL/sQTL) (gtex)
items.text:
• URL: https://gtexportal.org/home/downloads/adult-gtex/qtl
  • Access: Significant pairs open; full summary statistics via the GTEx/AnVIL buckets.
  • Format: Parquet / text, GRCh38
  • Build: GRCh38
  • Good for: Tissue QTLs for colocalisation.
  • Cite: GTEx Consortium. Science 2020;369:1318-1330.

items.title: eQTL Catalogue (eqtl-catalogue)
items.text:
• URL: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/eqtl/Data_access/
  • Access: Open via FTP (tabix-indexed per dataset). The old REST API is retired.
  • Format: Tab-separated, tabix-indexed, GRCh38
  • Build: GRCh38
  • Good for: Uniformly processed QTLs from many studies.
  • Cite: Kerimov N et al. Nat Genet 2021.

items.title: PGS Catalog (pgs-catalog)
items.text:
• URL: https://www.pgscatalog.org
  • Access: Open.
  • Format: Scoring files
  • Build: GRCh37/GRCh38 harmonised
  • Good for: Published polygenic score weights (not summary statistics).
  • Cite: Lambert SA et al. Nat Genet 2021.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
GeNor needs only uv:

curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

uv fetches a suitable Python and GeNor's dependencies on first use. Supported platforms: Linux and macOS (x86-64 and Apple silicon). On Windows, install uv inside WSL and follow the Linux instructions.

Until GeNor is on PyPI, replace genor in uvx genor ... with --from git+https://github.com/amanzadi/GeNor genor, e.g. uvx --from git+https://github.com/amanzadi/GeNor genor doctor.

Claude Code and Claude Desktop are the fully tested surfaces. Codex and opencode use the same MCP server and skills; they are smoke-tested only.

items.title: Claude Code (plugin)
items.text:
/plugin marketplace add amanzadi/GeNor
/plugin install genor@genor

or from a shell: claude plugin marketplace add amanzadi/GeNor && claude plugin install genor@genor.

The plugin provides:

  • the 12 GeNor skills (auto-loaded when relevant; start with genor)
  • the genor MCP server (uvx --from ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} genor mcp)
  • genor on the PATH of Claude's Bash tool (bin/genor, a thin uvx wrapper)
  • slash commands: /genor:doctor, /genor:pipeline, /genor:mr, /genor:rg, /genor:example

The first call builds GeNor's environment (about a minute); later calls start in seconds.

Without the plugin, use the CLI and copy the skills into the project:

uv tool install git+https://github.com/amanzadi/GeNor     # puts `genor` on PATH
genor skills install --agent claude                       # -> .claude/skills (or --scope user)
claude mcp add genor -- genor mcp                         # optional: MCP tools too

items.title: Claude Desktop
items.text:
Claude Desktop reaches GeNor through MCP only. Edit claude_desktop_config.json (Settings → Developer → Edit Config):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "genor": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--from", "git+https://github.com/amanzadi/GeNor", "genor", "mcp"],
      "env": { "GENOR_WORKDIR": "/Users/you/genor-workspace" }
    }
  }
}

Claude Desktop does not inherit your shell PATH: if uvx is not found, use its absolute path (which uvx, typically ~/.local/bin/uvx). GENOR_WORKDIR is where runs are written and where relative file paths are resolved; put your summary statistics there or give absolute paths.

Desktop chats have no skills, so the server tells the model to call get_guidance("genor") first; the skill text is served over MCP.

An experimental Desktop extension manifest is in packaging/mcpb/ (see its README).

items.title: Codex (CLI and desktop app)
items.text:
~/.codex/config.toml:

[mcp_servers.genor]
command = "uvx"
args = ["--from", "git+https://github.com/amanzadi/GeNor", "genor", "mcp"]
startup_timeout_sec = 120   # first start builds the environment
tool_timeout_sec = 60       # GeNor tools return within ~50 s and hand back job ids

[mcp_servers.genor.env]
GENOR_WORKDIR = "/home/you/genor-workspace"

Skills (Codex reads .agents/skills in the repo and ~/.agents/skills):

uvx --from git+https://github.com/amanzadi/GeNor genor skills install --agent codex            # project
uvx --from git+https://github.com/amanzadi/GeNor genor skills install --agent codex --scope user

If the Codex desktop app does not load skills, the MCP get_guidance tool serves the same text.

items.title: opencode
items.text:
opencode.json (project) or ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json. Recent opencode versions:

{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "genor": {
        "type": "local",
        "command": ["uvx", "--from", "git+https://github.com/amanzadi/GeNor", "genor", "mcp"]
      }
    }
  }
}

Older opencode versions put the server directly under "mcp" with "enabled": true; check opencode --version and its docs. Skills: genor skills install --agent opencode writes to .agents/skills, which opencode also reads.

items.title: Plain CLI
items.text:
uvx genor doctor                 # one-off
uv tool install genor            # persistent `genor` command
genor --help

items.title: Optional pieces
items.text:
Need Command Notes Clumping / LD genor backend install plink2 and genor refdata fetch g1000-eur --yes 288 MB panel LDSC genor refdata fetch ldsc-ldscores-eur ldsc-weights-eur 25 MB condFDR / conjFDR run GeNor on Python 3.13 with the pleioFDR port (below) 262 MB template + 2.4 GB reference, ~12 GB RAM MAGMA download from https://cncr.nl/research/magma/, then genor backend add magma /path/to/magma licence forbids bundling COJO, SMR binaries genor backend install gcta / smr commands that drive them are on the roadmap

pleioFDR (Python port, pinned commit):

uv tool install --python 3.13 git+https://github.com/amanzadi/GeNor \
  --with "pleiofdr @ git+https://github.com/espenhgn/pleiofdr@45e03b9c98c48ce9ef1496c4173a5581b23a853d"

items.title: Where things are stored
items.text:
What Default Override Reference data, downloaded binaries ~/Library/Application Support/genor (macOS), ~/.local/share/genor (Linux) GENOR_DATA_DIR or GENOR_HOME Backend registrations platform config dir GENOR_CONFIG_DIR Background jobs platform state dir GENOR_JOBS_DIR Run directories ./genor_runs/ or --out —

On a cluster, set GENOR_HOME=/shared/project/genor so reference data is downloaded once.

items.title: MCP tools
items.text: Generated by scripts/gen_cli_docs.py. Start the server with genor mcp (stdio). Analyses run as background jobs: tools wait up to wait_seconds (max 50, under Codex's 60 s default tool timeout) and otherwise return a job_id for job_status / job_result. Relative paths resolve against the workspace: $GENOR_WORKDIR, else the server's working directory (~/genor-workspace when that is /).

items.title: backend_add(name, path)
items.text: Register a tool the user installed themselves (e.g. MAGMA, whose licence forbids bundling). path is the executable (named as the registry expects, e.g. 'magma') or its directory.

items.title: backend_install(name, wait_seconds?)
items.text: Download a pinned redistributable binary: plink2, gcta or smr.

items.title: backend_list()
items.text: External tools (PLINK 2, GCTA, SMR, MAGMA, pleioFDR) and how to enable missing ones.

items.title: doctor()
items.text: Platform, available backends, downloaded reference data, and what each missing piece blocks. Call first.

items.title: example_data(out_dir?)
items.text: Copy the bundled simulated GWAS pair (BMI_sim exposure, MDD_sim outcome) into the workspace.

items.title: get_guidance(topic?)
items.text: GeNor skill text for clients without skills support. topic: 'genor' (start here), a workflow such as 'mendelian-randomisation', or '/references/.md'. No topic lists all topics.

items.title: job_cancel(job_id)
items.text: Cancel a running job.

items.title: job_logs(job_id, n?)
items.text: Last log lines of a job.

items.title: job_result(job_id, wait_seconds?)
items.text: Result JSON of a finished job (optionally wait up to wait_seconds).

items.title: job_status(job_id)
items.text: State of a background job: running, done, failed or cancelled.

items.title: list_methods()
items.text: Methods accepted by run_analysis and their parameters.

items.title: list_runs()
items.text: Run directories (with manifest.json) in the workspace.

items.title: lookup_enrichment(genes, background?, sources?)
items.text: g:Profiler functional enrichment (GO, Reactome, KEGG, HPA) with g:SCS correction.

items.title: lookup_genes_in_region(region, build?)
items.text: Genes overlapping chr:start-end (Ensembl), for positional mapping of loci.

items.title: lookup_open_targets(kind, query, n?, entity?)
items.text: Open Targets Platform. kind: search (free text), target (Ensembl gene ID), disease (EFO/MONDO ID), variant (GRCh38 CHR_POS_REF_ALT: credible sets + L2G), coloc (studyLocusId).

items.title: lookup_string(genes, required_score?)
items.text: STRING v12 interactions among genes and PPI enrichment p-value.

items.title: lookup_variants(rsids, build?)
items.text: Ensembl VEP: most severe consequence and genes for up to 200 rsIDs.

items.title: read_run(run_dir)
items.text: Short result of a run directory (result.json) plus the list of files it wrote.

items.title: refdata_fetch(name, confirmed_by_user?, allow_unpinned?, wait_seconds?)
items.text: Download a reference dataset. Datasets over 100 MB require the user's confirmation: ask them, then call with confirmed_by_user=true. A dataset without a pinned checksum (none at present) also needs allow_unpinned=true, again only after the user agrees.

items.title: refdata_list()
items.text: Reference datasets (LD scores, 1000G panels, chain files), sizes, and whether downloaded.

items.title: report_build(run_dirs, out?, title?)
items.text: Combine run directories into a Markdown + HTML report with warnings, decisions and citations. out must be inside the workspace.

items.title: run_analysis(method, params, wait_seconds?)
items.text: Run an analysis as a background job. method is one of: sumstats.load, sumstats.liftover, meta, ldsc.h2, ldsc.rg, clump, mr, pleio, finemap.abf, coloc.abf, magma.gene, magma.sets. params use the CLI option names with underscores (see list_methods). Returns the result if done within wait_seconds, else a job_id to poll.
Load a user's summary statistics file: detect columns, standardise, infer build, QC, plots. Returns the trait directory (pass it to other tools). Do not guess ancestry or N: ask the user.

items.title: sumstats_sources(name?)
items.text: Where users can download GWAS summary statistics (GWAS Catalog, PGC, OpenGWAS, FinnGen, Pan-UKB, ...). GeNor never downloads GWAS itself; the user downloads and gives a local path.

items.title: run_analysis methods
items.text: method CLI params sumstats.load genor sumstats load file, trait, out, build, ancestry, n, n_cases, n_controls, population_prevalence, effect_type, columns{canonical:filecol}, maf, info, drop_mhc sumstats.liftover genor sumstats liftover trait, to (GRCh37 meta genor meta run traits[list of trait dirs], scheme (ivw ldsc.h2 genor ldsc h2 trait, pop_prev, intercept, ref, w, out ldsc.rg genor ldsc rg trait1, trait2, pop_prev1, pop_prev2, out clump genor clump run trait, mode (plink mr genor mr run exposure, outcome, p_threshold, clump_mode (plink pleio genor pleio run trait1, trait2, stat (condfdr finemap.abf genor finemap abf trait, region (chr:start-end) or lead, window_kb, p1, level, out coloc.abf genor coloc abf trait1, trait2, region or lead, window_kb, p1, p2, p12, out magma.gene genor magma gene trait, gene_loc, ref_bfile, up_kb, down_kb, out magma.sets genor magma sets genes_raw, set_annot or covar, out

items.title: Methods, defaults and validation status
items.text: Each method lists its implementation, key defaults (with the reason), and how it is validated. The skills in skills/ explain interpretation and the decisions left to the user.

items.title: Summary statistics
items.text:
genor sumstats load: reads TSV/CSV/space-delimited text (optionally gzip/zip), Parquet and single-trait GWAS-VCF. Columns are detected from ~150 aliases (src/genor/sumstats/columns.py), including PLINK 2 .glm (A1 is the effect allele), REGENIE, SAIGE (Allele2 is the effect allele), BOLT-LMM, METAL, FinnGen and GWAS Catalog harmonised files. --col canonical=FILECOLUMN overrides.

  • Odds ratios become log-odds; a beta column that looks like odds ratios stops with a question.
  • Z from beta/SE; SE from beta and P when SE is missing; P from Z when P is missing.
  • Build inferred from ~4,000 marker SNPs with known GRCh37/GRCh38 positions.
  • Individual-level files (.bed/.pgen/.bgen/..., VCFs with genotypes) are refused.

QC defaults: MAF ≥ 0.01 (LD panels of ~500 people do not tag rarer variants), INFO ≥ 0.8, valid P/SE/beta/alleles, duplicates resolved by smallest P. Palindromic SNPs and the MHC are flagged, not removed. Reports λGC, λ1000, mean χ², genome-wide significant count.

Liftover: native UCSC chain-file liftover for SNP positions (no external tool). Variants mapping to the reverse strand or another chromosome are dropped and counted.

Validation: unit tests for each format, the refusal path, build inference, QC counts, allele harmonisation (aligned, swapped, strand-flipped, palindromic resolved by frequency, dropped).

items.title: Meta-analysis (genor meta run)
items.text:
Fixed-effect inverse-variance weighting (METAL SCHEME STDERR) with Cochran's Q, I² and DerSimonian-Laird random effects; or sample-size-weighted Z (METAL SCHEME SAMPLESIZE). Alleles are aligned to the first study reporting each variant.

Validation: identical to R meta::metagen (fixed, random, Q, I², τ²) to 1e-8 relative on a 60-variant, 3-study fixture.

items.title: LD score regression (genor ldsc h2, genor ldsc rg)
items.text:
Regression code vendored unmodified from CBIIT/ldsc (Python 3 port of bulik/ldsc, GPL-3). Data handling reproduces munge_sumstats.py (SNVs only, no strand- ambiguous SNPs, INFO > 0.9, MAF > 0.01, N ≥ N90/1.5) and ldsc.py (200 blocks; two-step estimator at χ² 30 for h2; reference-panel SNP order). Reference: 1000G Phase 3 EUR HapMap3 LD scores and weights from Zenodo 10515792 (CC BY 4.0).

Liability-scale h2 uses the sample prevalence from case/control counts and the user's population prevalence. Warnings: mean χ² < 1.02, h2 z < 4, intercept > 1.1 or < 0.95, rg outside [-1.2, 1.2], cross-trait intercept ≠ 0 (sample overlap).

Validation: identical to the original ldsc.py --h2/--rg (h2, rg, SEs, intercepts to 1e-6 relative) on the same munged input (tests/test_ldsc_golden.py, marked slow: downloads 25 MB).

items.title: Clumping (genor clump run)
items.text: PLINK 2 --clump per chromosome against 1000G Phase 3 EUR or EAS. Presets: loci (p 5e-8, r² 0.1, 250 kb), mr (p 5e-8, r² 0.001, 10 Mb). --mode distance keeps the strongest variant per window without LD, always with a distance_clumping warning.

items.title: Mendelian randomisation (genor mr run)
items.text:
Instrument selection (p < 5e-8, mr clumping), harmonisation (TwoSampleMR action 2: palindromes with MAF > 0.42 dropped), then: IVW (multiplicative random effects, main), IVW fixed effects, MR-Egger with intercept and I²_GX, weighted median (bootstrap SE), weighted and simple mode (bootstrap SE), Wald ratios, leave-one-out IVW, Cochran's Q (IVW and Egger), Steiger directionality, F statistics. Plots: scatter, forest, funnel, leave-one-out. STROBE-MR checklist with each of the 20 items marked filled / partial / human.

The analysis asks the user about sample overlap unless --overlap is given.

Validation against TwoSampleMR 0.7.14 on a 141-instrument fixture: IVW, IVW-FE, MR-Egger (slope, intercept, SEs, p, Q), Wald ratio and leave-one-out identical to 1e-8; weighted median and weighted/simple mode point estimates identical to 1e-6 (the mode uses a port of R's density()); bootstrap SEs agree within Monte Carlo error.

items.title: condFDR / conjFDR (genor pleio run)
items.text:
GeNor aligns each trait to pleioFDR's 9,545,380-SNP template (z signed to the template A1), writes logpvec/zvec MAT files and config.txt, and runs the pleioFDR Python port (commit 45e03b9), which is itself validated against the MATLAB version. Defaults: condFDR threshold 0.01, conjFDR 0.05, 500 random prunings, MHC excluded.

Validation: a round trip on the chr21 demo data (GeNor alignment of re-encoded traits, half with swapped alleles, vs pleioFDR on the original MAT files) gives identical result tables (scripts/golden/pleio_roundtrip.py).

items.title: Fine-mapping and colocalisation
items.text:
genor finemap abf: Wakefield approximate Bayes factors, one causal variant, prior 1e-4 per variant, prior effect SD 0.15·sdY (quantitative, sdY estimated from MAF and N as in coloc) or 0.2 (case-control); credible set conditional on a causal variant being present.

genor coloc abf: coloc ABF with p1 = p2 = 1e-4, p12 = 1e-5; reports PP.H0–H4 and per-SNP PP.H4.

Validation: identical to coloc::coloc.abf and coloc::finemap.abf (coloc 5.2.3) to 1e-6, both with supplied and estimated sdY.

items.title: Gene-level and lookups
items.text:
• MAGMA gene / gene-set / gene-property: drives a user-installed MAGMA (annotation window 35 kb up / 10 kb down by default).
  • Open Targets Platform GraphQL: search, target, disease, variant credible sets with L2G, colocalisations of a credible set.
  • Ensembl: VEP consequences (GRCh38 or GRCh37 server), genes overlapping a region.
  • STRING v12 (version-pinned URL, ≥ 1 s between requests): network and PPI enrichment.
  • g:Profiler: GO/Reactome/KEGG/HPA enrichment with g:SCS correction and optional custom background.

Validation: offline tests with recorded responses (tests/fixtures/http), and a nightly live job that checks the services still answer in the expected shape.

items.title: Reference data and external tools
items.text: Nothing is downloaded without a command. Methods that need missing data stop with refdata_missing (or backend_missing) and the exact command to run; downloads over 100 MB need --yes, so an agent has to ask you first. genor doctor shows what each missing piece blocks.

items.title: Reference datasets (genor refdata list | fetch | remove)
items.text:
Name Size Build Ancestry Used by Source / licence ldsc-ldscores-eur 13 MB GRCh37 EUR LDSC h2/rg Zenodo 10515792, CC BY 4.0 ldsc-weights-eur 12 MB GRCh37 EUR LDSC h2/rg Zenodo 10515792, CC BY 4.0 g1000-eur 288 MB GRCh37 EUR clumping Zenodo 10515792 (1000 Genomes, open) g1000-eas 323 MB GRCh37 EAS clumping Zenodo 10515792 (1000 Genomes, open) chain-hg19-to-hg38 0.2 MB — — liftover UCSC chain-hg38-to-hg19 1.2 MB — — liftover UCSC pleiofdr-template 262 MB GRCh37 EUR condFDR/conjFDR precimed pleiofdr-ref-eur 2.4 GB GRCh37 EUR condFDR/conjFDR precimed

Every entry has a pinned SHA-256 in src/genor/refdata/registry.toml; downloads that do not match are rejected. The pleioFDR files have no published checksum, so their pins are the hashes GeNor's maintainers saw on 2026-11-25. The SHA-256 seen is recorded in each run's manifest.

items.title: External tools (genor backend list | install | add | remove)
items.text:
Name Mode Platforms Used by plink2 (alpha 7, 2026-11-07) downloaded by GeNor, SHA-256 pinned Linux x86-64 (AVX2 or generic), macOS arm64 / x86-64 clumping gcta (1.95.4) downloaded, pinned Linux x86-64, macOS arm64 (COJO, roadmap) smr (1.4.3) downloaded, pinned Linux x86-64, macOS arm64 (SMR, roadmap) magma user installs (licence forbids redistribution) any genor magma pleiofdr Python package, pinned git commit, Python ≥ 3.13 any genor pleio

Resolution order: a path registered with genor backend add, then a binary GeNor downloaded, then PATH.

items.title: Roadmap
items.text: Release 0.1 covers milestones 1–3 of the plan (skeleton, sumstats, core statistics) plus the agent surfaces (skills, MCP server, Claude Code plugin) and parts of the locus and biology milestones (ABF fine-mapping, coloc ABF, MAGMA driver, Open Targets / Ensembl / STRING / g:Profiler lookups).

items.title: Next
items.text:
• Locus level: native SuSiE-RSS with LD from the 1000G panel (golden test vs susieR); coloc-SuSiE; GCTA-COJO driver (binary already pinned); SMR/HEIDI driver (binary pinned); eQTL Catalogue / GTEx v10 lookups over tabix (their REST APIs are retired).
  • Biology: FUMA-style SNP2GENE (positional + eQTL + L2G) in one command; MAGMA auxiliary files via refdata; gene-property (tissue / cell type) inputs.
  • LDSC: partitioned h2 (baselineLD v2.2) and LDSC-SEG; non-EUR LD scores.
  • Opt-in R backends (Rscript subprocess): susieR cross-check, MR-PRESSO, MVMR, CAUSE, LAVA.
  • MiXeR through Apptainer/Docker on x86-64 Linux.
  • PRS weights (PRS-CS, vendored MIT) and PGS Catalog lookup; no genotype scoring.
  • Release: PyPI (trusted publishing; needs the maintainer's PyPI project), docs site, recorded end-to-end agent demo, validated .mcpb Desktop extension.

items.title: Release gate
items.text:
1. uv run pytest and uv run pytest -m slow pass on Linux x86-64 and macOS arm64.
  2. Clean-machine run: uvx --from . genor doctor and the example pipeline with no R/conda/Docker.
  3. End-to-end on the example plus two public traits downloaded by hand (e.g. PGC MDD and a GWAS Catalog BMI study); report inspected by hand.
  4. Agent test in Claude Code (plugin) and Claude Desktop (MCP only): "estimate the genetic correlation and causal effect of BMI on depression from these two files" completes and stops to ask about ancestry, prevalence, sample overlap and large downloads. Codex and opencode: smoke run of the same prompt.

items.title: Validation
items.text:
Native reimplementations are the main correctness risk, so each is compared with the reference tool on fixed inputs. Reference values are stored in tests/golden/ and regenerated by scripts in scripts/golden/.

GeNor Reference Fixture Agreement Test MR: IVW, IVW-FE, Egger, Wald, leave-one-out TwoSampleMR 0.7.14 141 harmonised instruments 1e-8 relative tests/test_golden.py MR: weighted median, weighted/simple mode (point) TwoSampleMR 0.7.14 same 1e-6 relative same MR: bootstrap SEs TwoSampleMR 0.7.14 same within Monte Carlo error (15–30%) same coloc ABF, finemap ABF coloc 5.2.3 300-SNP simulated region 1e-6 relative same Meta-analysis fixed/random, Q, I², τ² R meta 9.0.0 (metagen, DL) 3 studies × 60 variants 1e-8 relative same LDSC h2, rg, SEs, intercepts original ldsc.py (CBIIT/ldsc ldsc313 @ 128f996) munged example traits 1e-6 relative tests/test_ldsc_golden.py (slow) condFDR via pleioFDR port pleioFDR port on original demo MAT files chr21 demo, alleles re-encoded identical tables scripts/golden/pleio_roundtrip.py

Regenerating:

Rscript scripts/golden/make_golden.R                 # needs TwoSampleMR, coloc, meta, jsonlite
python scripts/golden/ldsc_reference.py <ldsc checkout> <refdata dir>
python scripts/golden/pleio_roundtrip.py             # in a folder with the pleioFDR demo + template

items.title: End-to-end check on simulated data
items.text: genor example ships data simulated from the real 1000G HapMap3 LD-score structure with known parameters (truth.json). On it, LDSC rg is 0.142 ± 0.032 (truth 0.15), IVW MR 0.136 ± 0.018 (truth 0.15), weighted median 0.147 and weighted mode 0.152, and the three planted pleiotropic instruments trigger the heterogeneity and Egger-intercept warnings. tests/test_pipeline.py checks the MR estimate stays within 3 SE of the truth.

items.title: Not validated yet
items.text:
• PLINK clumping output is PLINK's; GeNor's part (per-chromosome runs, panel selection, guards) is covered by the example run, not a golden test.
  • MAGMA wrapping has no automated test (MAGMA cannot be installed in CI).
  • The release-gate agent test (Claude Code and Claude Desktop completing "estimate the genetic correlation and causal effect of BMI on depression" with the right stop-and-ask points) is a manual checklist before each release.
